newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dlr ends up before G7 summit, stocks mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dlr ends up before G7 summit, stocks mixed.

text.p: The dollar held its gains against the yen on Friday after President Bill Clinton helped reassure markets that a summit of leading industrial nations would not become a forum for a U.S.-Japan trade row.

European bourses ended the week in a mixed mood. Frankfurt closed at a record high, helped by the dollar, but London finished with losses of 1.3 percent as fears of higher interest rates gripped the market.

On currency markets, sterling was the biggest mover, posting a fresh 58-month high against the mark on the prospect of higher near-term British interest rates, but most interest focused on the dollar.

The U.S. currency ended the day up half a yen as world leaders gathered for the three-day meeting of the Group of Seven (G7) in Denver. Remarks by Clinton quietened market talk that Washington would attack Tokyo at the talks because of the recent jump in its trade surplus.
Exchange rates are a sensitive issue in Japanese-American relations because a strong dollar helps Tokyo's exports to the United States.

But dealers said the potential for friction dissipated after Thursday's smaller-than-expected U.S. April trade deficit and comments overnight from Clinton and Japanese Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto.
"The Clinton-Hashimoto talks look to have taken a lot of the heat out of the meeting," said Peter Wood, forex dealer at Bank of Boston. "And we don't expect to see too much grousing about forex."

Clinton voiced concern about Japan's rising merchandise trade surplus, which rose more than 200 percent in May, but added that foreign exchange rates should not be used as tools to manipulate trade imbalances, U.S. officials said.
Currency dealers saw this as a signal that the Clinton administration would not resort to calls for a weaker dollar to help to redress the trade imbalance, as it has done in the past.

"I expect the G7 to make a very neutral foreign exchange statement and it will probably have limited impact on trade," said Mike Malpede, senior foreign exchange analyst at Refco Group Ltd in New York.
"But it probably opens the dollar up for a little bit of dollar buying against the yen," he added.

The dollar was at 114.62 yen in late European trade, compared with 114.09 on Thursday. Concern that Denver would become the setting for a row had driven the dollar down as low as 112.75 earlier this week.
In contrast, a long rally by the dollar reached a four-and-a-half year high of 127.46 yen on May 1.

The stronger dollar helped boost some European bourses. Frankfurt floor trade ended at a new peak, up 39 points to 3,788.27 on the DAX index, although gains on the after-hours IBIS index were modest after earlier touching a trading high at 3,801.35 points.
"The market is still in very good shape," said one trader. The recent strong performance on Wall Street has been the driving factor for the German share market.
"The market is more focused on the U.S. right now instead of on domestic factors," said another trader.
London, Europe's biggest share market, ended a week of constant retreat with another heavy fall, registering losses of 1.3 percent on the blue-chip FTSE index at the close.
"There's no guts in the market and nothing to go for," said one dealer.
The London market, which has fallen 140 points in the past week, has been dogged by worries over higher interest rates to dampen inflationary pressures.
It has also been unsettled by persistent press reports that finance minister Gordon Brown will scrap a tax break on dividend payments to major corporate investors.
In Paris, stocks closed with gains but trade was thin with investors digesting the implications of Prime Minister Lionel Jospin's first major policy address on Thursday.

"There's not a lot of interest or a lot of volume," a broker said. "Although we were expecting some clarifications, a lot of doubt remains. A lot of decisions have been put off to September so uncertainty persists."
CURRENCIES AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
The dollar was at 1.7300 marks and 114.62 yen, compared with 1.7247 and 114.09 in late European trade on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS AT THE EUROPEAN CLOSE
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index finished down 59.8 points at 4,593.9.
PARIS - The CAC-40 closed up 17.41 points at 2,757.10.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index ended floor trade up 39.00 points at 3,788.27.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold finished at a $338.45 an ounce low, against $339.75 on Thursday. Silver was barely changed at $4.76 in late trade.
